endorsements.quote: Diverse representation within research teams can thus help bring to light potential limitations in these assumptions, particularly regarding how certain rules or variables may unintentionally exclude or disadvantage specific groups.

The protocol also encourages researchers to document their rationale for problem definition and the selection of proxy variables, reflect on how problem framing aligns with intended outcomes, evaluate how closely the proxies approximate the true variables of interest, and implement measures to mitigate any foreseeable risks.

unlisted_practices: AI development teams should adopt a Team Card documenting team composition, positionality, and steps taken to monitor and address unconscious bias.
Development teams should practice reflexivity, or critical self-reflection on their positionality, throughout the AI development lifecycle.
Development teams should cultivate epistemic diversity through active, collaborative, interdisciplinary processes rather than relying on social diversity alone.
Development teams should update Team Cards periodically and acknowledge prior contributors.
Development teams should prepare multiple modular Team Cards for discrete lifecycle stages, with a record linking them, when projects involve multiple teams.
Development teams reusing pre-existing or open-source models should transparently discuss the appropriateness of the materials and mitigate legacy bias.
Developers should test and validate AI tools in the geographic contexts where they will be deployed.
Developers should design AI development processes that anticipate formal review and approval by an IRB or ethics committee.
Regulators should collaborate internationally to intensify scrutiny of datasets used to train medical AI systems deployed across diverse geographic and social contexts.
Development teams should include end-user advocates, such as physicians and patient advocates, and ethical oversight and regulatory compliance functions.

screen.reason: The paper introduces a conceptual framework/protocol (the Team Card) for governance and mitigating bias in medical AI by documenting team positionality and diversity. It does not conduct an empirical evaluation comparing outcomes.
